---
title: "Packaging & Project Setup"
description: "How projects are packaged: pyproject.toml, versions, layout, dependencies, metadata, typing, linting, and the Makefile."
---

## 1. `pyproject.toml` is the single source of truth
- There is no `setup.py` or `setup.cfg`. The only exception is when a compiled extension needs
  one (multimark uses a CFFI build).
- Project metadata, dependencies, extras, and the ruff, pytest, coverage and pyright settings all
  live in `pyproject.toml`.

## 2. Versions come from git tags, not from a hard-coded string
- The build uses setuptools with `setuptools_scm` and `dynamic = ["version"]`:
  ```toml
  [build-system]
  requires = ["setuptools>=77", "setuptools_scm>=8"]
  build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

  [project]
  dynamic = ["version"]

  [tool.setuptools_scm]
  ```
- A release is just a tag (`v0.7.0`) plus a GitHub Release. Nobody has to remember to bump a
  version string.
- At runtime, `__version__` is read from the installed metadata, with a fallback:
  ```python
  from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version
  try:
      __version__ = version("mypkg")
  except PackageNotFoundError:  # pragma: no cover
      __version__ = "0.0.0"
  ```
- CI checks out the repo with `fetch-depth: 0` so that setuptools_scm can see the tags.
- The Rust package (GridWell) uses **maturin** with `abi3` wheels instead, so one wheel
  per platform covers every Python version.

## 3. Flat layout with explicit package discovery
```toml
[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["mypkg", "mypkg.*"]
```
- Explicit discovery means stray folders such as `tests/`, `scripts/` or `user_guide/` never get
  shipped by accident.

## 4. Support a modern Python floor and test the whole range
- `requires-python = ">=3.10"` is the norm.
- Classifiers list every supported minor version, 3.10 through 3.14.
- The CI matrix tests that same range.
- Code uses modern syntax (`X | None`, built-in generics) throughout.

## 5. Keep hard dependencies small, with lower bounds only
- Dependencies get `>=` lower bounds and no upper caps. Caps cause resolver conflicts for
  downstream users.
- When an upper bound or pin is truly necessary, it gets a comment saying why:
  ```toml
  "sqlglot>=23.4,<30.18",  # sqlglot 30.18+ breaks DROP statements
  ```
- Heavy or optional functionality goes into extras. pandas and polars are never hard
  dependencies when they can be avoided. The current template's core set is just
  `narwhals`, `numpy`, `scipy` and `typing_extensions`.

## 6. Short, predictable extras names
- `pd`, `pl`, `pa` install the pandas, polars and pyarrow backends.
- Feature extras are named after what they enable: `altair`, `tables`, `formula`, `fast`
  (numba), `mcp`.
- `docs` installs Great Docs.
- `dev` installs pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, pyright, build, and the backend extras.
- `all` is self-referencing: `all = ["mypkg[pd,pl,pa,altair,tables]"]`.
- Error messages tell users which extra to install, e.g. `pip install "mypkg[pl]"`.

## 7. Complete, accurate metadata
- `authors` and `maintainers` (with email), `license = { file = "LICENSE" }`, `keywords`, and
  classifiers covering Development Status, Intended Audience, Topic, Python versions and
  `Typing :: Typed`.
- `[project.urls]` uses a consistent four-key set:
  ```toml
  [project.urls]
  Homepage = "..."
  Repository = "..."
  Documentation = "..."
  "Bug Tracker" = "..."
  ```
- The license is MIT, the same choice in every project.

## 8. Ship type information
- Packages include a `py.typed` marker and list it explicitly in package data:
  ```toml
  [tool.setuptools.package-data]
  mypkg = ["py.typed"]
  ```
- pyright runs in **strict** mode, configured in `pyproject.toml`. Only the noisy
  "unknown type" family of checks is relaxed, because numpy and scipy stubs trigger it
  constantly.

## 9. Use ruff for both linting and formatting, at line length 100
```toml
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM"]
```
- A single tool replaces black, isort, flake8 and pyupgrade.
- **pre-commit** runs ruff and the basic hygiene hooks (trailing whitespace, end-of-file).
  The ruff version in pre-commit is pinned to match the one in the `dev` extra, with a comment
  telling you to bump both together.

## 10. A self-documenting Makefile as the developer interface
- Every project has the same targets, so moving between repos needs no re-learning:
  ```make
  help:        ## Show this help message (awk over the "## " comments)
  install:     ## pip install -e ".[dev]"
  test:        ## pytest with coverage
  lint:        ## ruff format + ruff check --fix
  check-format:## ruff format --check + ruff check
  type-check:  ## pyright mypkg
  check: lint type-check test   ## the pre-push gate
  build:       ## python -m build
  docs:        ## great-docs build
  docs-preview:## great-docs preview
  clean:       ## clean-build clean-pyc clean-test
  ```
- `make help` lists all targets, generated from the `## ` comments on each line.
